title: Death at the Meridian Observatory
tagline: A director falls from the great telescope on the night of the donor gala. Nobody saw a thing. Everybody is lying about something.
setting: The Meridian Observatory, a privately funded mountain observatory, on the night of its annual donor gala.
briefing: At 23:40 on Saturday night, security guard Nell Okafor found the observatory's director, Dr. Elias Voss (58), dead on the floor of the main dome beneath the telescope gantry. The donor gala had been running in the hall next door since 19:00. Voss was last seen leaving the hall at about 22:25. First responders assumed a fall on the gantry stairs. Three people had reason to quarrel with him that night: his deputy director Dr. Mara Quill, his doctoral student Theo Lark, and board chairman and principal donor Gideon Ashby. The dome corridor camera was not recording. Whether this is an accident or a homicide — and who, if anyone, should answer for it — is for the investigation to establish.

victim.name: Dr. Elias Voss
victim.description: Director of the Meridian Observatory, 58. Brilliant, exacting, and not well liked.

seats.title: Prosecutor
seats.blurb: Decides whether and whom to charge, then must prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.

seats.title: Defense Counsel
seats.blurb: Represents whoever is charged: suppression motions, cross-examination, and the alternative theory.

seats.title: Presiding Judge
seats.blurb: Rules on warrants, motions, and objections; keeps the trial fair; passes sentence.

procedure.standard: Guilt must be proved beyond reasonable doubt on the admitted record. Evidence that was suppressed or excluded, and testimony that was struck, must not be considered. A unanimous jury is required to convict or acquit.
